tagline.text: Off-road ATV rides on the dirt tracks between the Chocolate Hills in Carmen

location.label: Location
location.text: Buenos Aires, Carmen, Bohol (near the Chocolate Hills Complex)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours (half a day including round-trip transfers)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,600 (per ATV, 30 minutes to 2 hours; transport and entrance fee extra)

children.text: This is an off-road experience in Carmen, Bohol, riding an ATV along dirt tracks, rice fields and villages between the Chocolate Hills. Courses run from 30 minutes to 2 hours, and beginners can ride with a guide.

The Bohol ATV adventure is an activity in Carmen, in central Bohol, where you ride a four-wheeled ATV or a buggy along the dirt roads around the Chocolate Hills. The best-known starting point is the cluster of ATV rental yards in Barangay Buenos Aires, close to the Chocolate Hills Complex, and on OpenStreetMap this village sits just south of the complex.

The Chocolate Hills are a group of conical limestone hills rising in central Bohol, and Wikipedia says the estimated number of hills ranges from 1,268 to 1,776. Most visitors simply look down on the scenery from the viewing deck, but an ATV course takes you along farm roads, rice paddy dikes, banana groves and village lanes, so you see the same landscape from ground level. One operator says some sections even include forest trails and shallow stream crossings.

The point that confuses first-time visitors most is that there is no single company called "Chocolate Hills ATV." Carmen has several rental yards and tour companies, and the booking sites that sell hotel-pickup packages mostly connect to those local operators. Even at the same location, the pricing basis (per vehicle or per person), inclusions, age rules and course length can differ, so compare conditions rather than names. This guide does not promote any single local business and names operators only where needed to confirm information. Courses and prices vary by operator and some do not publish a rate card, so this guide is based on the ranges that several operators have in common. Published examples are roughly
for 30 minutes,
for 1 hour and
for 2 hours per ATV, and a buggy costs double the ATV price and carries two people. Always confirm the exact amount with the operator before you book.

A very common plan, including among Korean travelers, is to add one hour of ATV riding to a Bohol countryside tour (Chocolate Hills, tarsiers and a Loboc River cruise). Because the round trip from Panglao or Tagbilaran takes a long time, we recommend leaving early, doing the ATV ride and the viewing deck first, and heading to the other sights in the afternoon.

blocks.title: Farm-road course between the Chocolate Hills

children.text: You follow a guide along dirt tracks, rice fields and banana groves between the conical hills. In the dry season the hills turn brown and match their name, while in the rainy season you see vivid green hills.
First-timers usually start with a
30-minute
or
1-hour
course and move up to the
2-hour
course that goes deeper once they are comfortable. One booking site also mentions a course of up to
4 hours
, but its price could not be confirmed, so check on site.
If you are nervous about driving an ATV yourself or are traveling with young children, you can choose a buggy. One operator says a buggy carries two people and costs double the ATV price.
Most operators give a short briefing on the controls and safety before departure and lend helmets and protective gear. A guide rides ahead and points out the route and viewpoints.

Some listings mention three or four viewpoint stops along the course for photos. One operator includes the Bud Agta viewpoint, whose staircase was demolished so that it can now be reached only by ATV.
Because you ride past small villages, farmhouses and rice fields in Carmen, you get a close look at everyday rural life in Bohol. Children often wave, so ride slowly when passing.

Several booking sites sell one-day tours built like this. Some reviewers say the ATV time was shorter than promised, so confirm the included time and stops in writing before you book.
Leave your hotel early for Carmen. Arriving early helps you avoid the heat and the waiting.
At the yard you receive a map, safety gear and a short briefing on the controls. Check the brakes, steering and fuel level yourself.
Start the
2-hour

Return the equipment, change clothes and drink plenty of water.
Head to the Chocolate Hills viewing deck or a nearby restaurant for lunch.
Self-drive rental is described as receiving a map and gear and riding on your own. If this is your first time, we recommend a guided course.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG), taking about
1 hour 30 minutes–1 hour 40 minutes
(per airline timetables). Airlines and schedules change often, so check the latest timetable.
You can also fly from Manila to Cebu and take a ferry from Cebu port to Tagbilaran.
Ferry times and fares differ by operator, so check the latest notices before you leave.
It is about
from Tagbilaran to the Chocolate Hills in Carmen. Guides say it takes about
1 hour 15 minutes–1 hour 30 minutes
by motorbike and about
1 hour 30 minutes
from Panglao.
Most travelers use a tour with hotel pickup or rent a car for the day. One operator's car rental examples are
for a sedan and
for an MPV (for 8 hours; confirm whether fuel is included).
Local buses run from Tagbilaran toward Carmen and are said to take about
1–2.5 hours
. Check the schedule and boarding point on site. You also need to work out in advance how to get from the bus stop to the ATV yard.
For short trips within Carmen you can use a tricycle or a motorcycle taxi, but check fares on site.

In the dry season the dirt tracks are firm and the hills turn brown, so it is the most popular time for ATV riding, but it is very dusty. In the rainy season the hills are a vivid green, but the tracks turn muddy and slippery, so take extra care.
During the day, mornings are cooler and the light is better for photos. Late afternoon also has soft light, but you must finish the course before sunset.

There are few places to stay around the ATV yards, so most travelers stay in Panglao or Tagbilaran and make a day trip. Around the Chocolate Hills Complex in Carmen there are small restaurants and souvenir shops where you can have a simple meal.

After riding you will be dusty and sweaty, so be sure to bring a change of clothes and a towel. Lunch is most often combined with a Loboc River buffet cruise, and cruise packages are described as including a buffet lunch, drinks and music.

Before booking, confirm the course time and inclusions (helmet, raincoat, fuel, guide, entrance fee) by message or in writing. Some reviewers complain that a 1-hour course was cut to about 35 minutes.

Minimum age rules vary a lot by operator. One says age 12 and over with a guardian, another lets riders drive from age 9, and some resale sites list 16 and over. If you are going with children, confirm directly.
Long pants and closed shoes are essential, and sandals or flip-flops are dangerous. Wear clothes you do not mind getting dirty.
Keep your phone in a waterproof bag or a zipped pocket, and a neck lanyard helps prevent drops on rough ground.
It is dusty, so a mask or buff and sunglasses help, especially in the dry season.
Many operators say you can ride without ATV experience if you follow the guide, but start slowly and keep a distance from the vehicle ahead.
Always check whether the ATV price is per vehicle or per person. Self-drive hire is mostly per vehicle and guided packages are mostly per person.
Bring plenty of cash in pesos. Many places do not accept cards for entrance fees and on-site payments.
ATV time is usually counted as actual riding time, excluding check-in and putting on gear. When planning, allow generous time for transfers and waiting.
If the ATV ride is your first stop of the day, you will arrive at the next stop covered in dust, so bring spare clothes and wet wipes.
ATV riding carries a risk of accidents. Always wear a helmet and do not ride if the equipment looks unsafe. Check before you leave whether your travel insurance covers ATV riding.
One review reported problems with steering and brakes. Test the brakes and steering yourself before departure.
In the rainy season the tracks are slippery and the risk of rollovers rises, so slow down and follow the guide's instructions.
Never drive after drinking alcohol.
The Chocolate Hills are a protected area, so do not ride off the course and do not litter.
Entrance fees and prices can change, so check the latest notices.
Courses may mix protected areas and private land, so do not ride off the route the guide sets.
The best-known viewing deck, said to be about a
5-minute
walk from the ATV starting point. Climb the 214 steps to look down over Bohol's hills.
A river famous for its buffet lunch cruises, often combined with ATV riding on Bohol countryside tours. Travel time from Carmen needs to be confirmed on site.
A place to see tarsiers, among the smallest primates in the world, and often included in one-day ATV tours.
A mahogany forest road you pass on the way to the Chocolate Hills, popular for photos. Tours often stop here in transit.
